title: Atlantic Fellows for Equity in Brain Health 2027-2028
organization: Global Brain Health Institute (GBHI) - Trinity College Dublin & UCSF
location: Dublin, Ireland or San Francisco, USA
eligibility: Open to applicants from any country including Uganda working on brain health, dementia prevention or related equity issues - neurologists, geriatricians, psychologists, nurses, public health and allied professionals. English proficiency required.
summary: A fully funded, 12-month interdisciplinary leadership fellowship protecting aging populations from threats to brain health, hosted at GBHI in Dublin or San Francisco. Applications for the 2027-2028 cohort close November 2, 2026.
description: GBHI brings together more than 300 Atlantic Fellows from over 65 countries to train leaders who reduce the scale and impact of dementia and inequities in brain health. Fellows receive full funding covering program costs, salary support/stipend, relocation and travel, plus academic training, mentorship, project support and lifelong membership in the Atlantic Fellows community. The program blends clinical, public health, policy and creative approaches to brain health equity. It suits mid-career clinicians, researchers, advocates and innovators from low- and middle-income countries who will return home to scale interventions.
how_to_apply: Complete the online GBHI application with CV, statements of interest and project proposal, and referee contacts by November 2, 2026.

title: AU Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme 2026/2027 - Cohort 2
eligibility: Youth- and women-led small enterprises registered and operating in an AU Member State (including Uganda) for at least two years, employing at least three full-time staff. Health enterprises are explicitly covered under the Services Cluster.
summary: The African Union's flagship MSME accelerator fellowship provides 100 fellows from all AU member states with 12 months of structured training, expert mentorship, IP support and AfCFTA market-access opportunities. Applications close September 30, 2026.
description: The EAN Fellowship is an AUC Startup Acceleration Initiative targeting USD 2 million in new attributable revenue and 500 new jobs across Cohort 2. All fellows receive twelve months of training across ten modules, mentorship through AU partners, access to the African Trade Observatory and AfCFTA market-intelligence tools, and participation in continental events. Seven sectors are covered, including Health, making this relevant for Ugandan health-innovation ventures, clinics, medtech and health-services SMEs. The inaugural cohort trained 56 fellows from 30 countries and generated over USD 1 million in deals. Women-led enterprises are especially encouraged.
how_to_apply: Submit the online form (business registration details, sector, pitch of up to 800 words) via the application form by September 30, 2026; shortlisted applicants later provide one finance-access document.

title: Fast Forward Accelerator 2027 for Tech Nonprofits
eligibility: Open to founders worldwide including Uganda building software-based nonprofits. Two hard requirements: pursuing a nonprofit business model and having at least a minimum viable product (MVP) built.
summary: A three-month accelerator giving tech nonprofits $25K+ in unrestricted seed capital, fundraising coaching, expert mentorship and a founder community. Applications for the 2027 cohort close September 7, 2026.
description: Fast Forward has accelerated 100+ tech nonprofits since 2014 and focuses on the unique needs of mission-driven technology organizations. Fellows refine their fundraising pitch, strengthen teams and scale impact through curriculum spanning board development, impact measurement, product strategy and go-to-market. Benefits include $25K+ unrestricted funding, mentorship from tech and social-impact leaders, investor/donor connections and a lifelong portfolio community. Digital-health nonprofits led by Ugandan clinicians or public health innovators fit squarely within scope; lived experience of the problem addressed is valued in selection.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application describing your MVP, team and impact model at apply.ffwd.org by September 7, 2026.

title: Melton Foundation Global Solvers Accelerator 2027
eligibility: Changemakers aged 20-35 from any country, including Uganda, actively leading a concrete community or social-impact project (health projects qualify) that continues through the program. English proficiency required.
summary: An eight-month virtual leadership and peer-learning accelerator for social impact leaders worldwide, culminating in a funded in-person Co-Lab and induction into the lifelong Melton Fellowship. Applications close November 15, 2026.
description: The Global Solvers Accelerator connects grassroots changemakers to re-engineer their community projects for greater impact through cross-boundary collaboration, personalized support and practical tools aligned to the SDGs. Participants commit roughly four hours weekly from April to November 2027, join learning labs and peer coaching, and attend the in-person Co-Lab (tentatively July 19-26, 2027), with costs covered for engaged participants. A program fee of USD 900 applies if selected, with partial need-based financial support available upon request during the application. Health-equity, community health and health-rights projects are common among cohorts.
how_to_apply: Apply online between August 15 and November 15, 2026; request need-based fee support within the original application; shortlisted candidates attend a virtual Assessment Centre around late January 2027.

title: Acumen Academy East Africa Fellowship (Next Intake)
location: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Burundi, South Sudan, Somalia)
eligibility: Citizens/residents of eligible East African countries including Uganda with at least 5 years of work experience, currently leading or building an organization addressing poverty full-time; women encouraged. No prior Acumen Fellowship participation.
summary: A fully funded, six-month hybrid moral-leadership program for East African change agents, combining virtual seminars with in-person immersives in cities like Nairobi and Kampala. New intakes announced periodically - join the notification list.
description: The East Africa Acumen Fellowship develops adaptive leadership, authentic voice and values-based decision-making through cohort-based seminars, self-paced assignments and peer coaching, with all program costs, lodging and food covered by Acumen. Alumni join the Foundry, a 1,600+ global community offering tools, coaching, amplification, and access to early-stage catalytic capital. Notable Ugandan alumni include Village Energy co-founder Abu Musuuza. Because intake windows vary by year and track, interested Ugandan health entrepreneurs should join Acumen's mailing list and verify the next call directly.
how_to_apply: Join the notification list on the fellowship page; when applications open, read the Applicant Toolkit, submit the online application (essays on your poverty-solving work), then participate in the Selection Conference if shortlisted.
key_dates: New intakes announced periodically; watch for next call

title: Kofi Annan Fellowship in Global Health Leadership (Next Cohort)
location: Africa-wide (residential sessions at AU/Africa CDC venues)
eligibility: Citizens of AU Member States including Uganda holding a postgraduate degree in a relevant public health field with at least 10 years of professional experience after the Masters; employer support letter required. Cohorts prioritize SRH and public mental health experts.
summary: Africa CDC's premier 12-month executive leadership fellowship builds the 'new public health order' generation, with five cohorts (109 fellows from 34 countries) graduated and all costs covered. The next cohort call is expected toward the end of 2026.
description: Fellows undertake high-level leadership training, mentorship and practical exposure to complex regional and global health challenges, leading implementation of Africa's Health Security and Sovereignty Agenda. Africa CDC covers travel, daily allowances and insurance during residential sessions, and alumni have risen to cabinet-level and senior institutional roles across the continent. Required materials typically include an employer support letter, two recommendation letters, a personal statement (max 400 words) and a leadership challenge project proposal. Ugandan public health leaders should monitor africacdc.org and jobs.au.int for the next call.
how_to_apply: Watch africacdc.org and jobs.au.int for the next cohort announcement; prepare employer support letter, two recommendations, personal statement and leadership project proposal for online submission when the call opens.

title: Aspen Institute New Voices Fellowship (Next Window)
organization: Aspen Institute - Aspen Global Innovators Group
eligibility: Locally-rooted development and health experts - scientists, physicians, advocates, journalists - from developing countries including Uganda, with significant professional achievement and a desire to engage international media.
summary: A year-long media, communication and advocacy fellowship that equips frontline health and development experts to shape global discourse, with 187 fellows from 40+ countries to date. Entry windows open periodically - currently not accepting applications.
description: New Voices provides world-class communications training, media coaching, op-ed development, speaking platforms such as Aspen Ideas Health, and ongoing alumni amplification. All fellowship-related costs and media-related travel are covered by the Aspen Institute. Many fellows are physicians, public health researchers and health journalists from East Africa who go on to influence national and global policy conversations. Windows have typically opened mid-year with fall deadlines; interested Ugandans should sign up for AGI updates and prepare nomination materials in advance.
how_to_apply: Sign up for Aspen Global Innovators updates; when nominations/applications reopen, submit the nomination/application form with CV, evidence of professional achievement and communication samples.
key_dates: Windows typically open mid-year; currently closed - watch for reopening

title: Obama Foundation Leaders Africa Program (2027-2028 Cycle)
eligibility: Leaders aged 24-45 who are citizens, permanent residents, or 5+ year residents of any African country including Uganda, with 3+ years relevant issue-area experience and professional English proficiency.
summary: A free, six-month values-based virtual leadership program with group sessions, peer community groups and individualized coaching, connecting participants to the 1,500+ Obama Leadership Network. The next cycle's application historically opens November-December.
description: Leaders Africa convenes exceptional leaders from public, civil society and private sectors to deepen ethical leadership skills through interactive plenaries, breakout work and monthly peer groups, each participant paired with a professional leadership coach. The program runs roughly September to May and requires abstaining from electoral campaigns during participation. There is no cost to participate. Ugandan health-sector leaders should monitor the official page and subscribe for notifications ahead of the next application window.
how_to_apply: Sign up for Obama Foundation emails; when the next application opens at obama.embark.com, complete eligibility questions, essays on your issue focus and impact, and submit before the stated deadline.
key_dates: Next application expected to open Nov-Dec 2026

title: EAC-KfW Master's Scholarships (Cohort 4) - Inter-University Council for East Africa
organization: Inter-University Council for East Africa (IUCEA) / East African Community / KfW
location: East African Community Partner States (study outside home country)
eligibility: Citizens of any of the 8 EAC Partner States (incl. Uganda) under 35 with a Bachelor's degree at Second Class Upper or better, applying for a Master's in another EAC Partner State.
summary: Up to 120 fully funded two-year master's scholarships under the EAC Scholarship Programme, funded by Germany (KfW). Ugandans study in Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and beyond. Deadline: September 10, 2026.
description: The EAC Scholarship Programme is a regional initiative of the East African Community and the Federal Republic of Germany implemented by IUCEA. The package includes full tuition paid to the host university, return air ticket, EUR 380 monthly stipend, EUR 200 arrival allowance, EUR 650 study materials allowance, EUR 1,500 study/research allowance, medical insurance and visa/entry fees. Applicants must apply for admission to an eligible master's programme at a partner university in another EAC country and submit a complete online application by 10 September 2026, 17:00 EAT. Health sciences and public health fields are eligible disciplines.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an eligible partner-university master's programme, then complete the online EAC Scholarship Application Form with all supporting documents before 17:00 EAT, 10 Sept 2026.

title: ARES International Training Scholarships in Belgium 2027-2028
organization: Academie de Recherche et d'Enseignement Superieur (ARES)
eligibility: Permanent residents and workers in one of 32 eligible ARES partner countries (Uganda explicitly listed) holding a higher education degree obtained within the last 20 years plus at least two years of relevant professional experience.
summary: 100 funded scholarships for one specialised bachelor's, eight specialised master's degrees or one six-month continuing education course in Belgium, including public-health-oriented programmes. Applications close September 18, 2026.
description: Programmes include the Specialised Master in Public Health Sciences (analysis and evaluation of international health policies, programmes and systems) and the Specialised Master in Integrated Management of Health Risks, alongside economics, human rights, food safety and disaster management options. Funding covers international travel, living allowance, insurance, registration fees and visa cost support. Candidates must apply for only one programme, in its language of instruction, and demonstrate good written/spoken proficiency. New GIRAF platform accounts must be created by 4 September 2026; final applications are due 18 September 2026 at noon Belgian time, with results by June 2027.
how_to_apply: Create a GIRAF account by 4 Sept 2026, select one programme, upload academic transcripts, proof of professional experience and language evidence, and submit before 18 Sept 2026 (12:00 Belgian time).

title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program - 2027 Intakes
organization: African Development Bank (AfDB) & Government of Japan
location: Japan (partner universities incl. Univ. of Tokyo, Kyoto, APU, Sophia, Hiroshima)
eligibility: Nationals of AfDB regional member countries (incl. Uganda) aged 35 or under with a bachelor's degree, at least one year of relevant work experience, and admission to an eligible master's programme at a JADS partner university.
summary: Fully funded two-year master's scholarships in Japan covering tuition, monthly stipend, airfare and insurance; health is an eligible field. Apply through partner universities - e.g., Ritsumeikan APU's April 2027 intake closes September 15, 2026.
description: JADS builds African human-resources capacity aligned with AfDB's High 5 priorities; scholars must return home after graduation to contribute to national development. There is no direct application to AfDB: candidates apply for admission to a JADS partner university, request scholarship consideration within that application, and the university endorses shortlisted candidates to the Bank. Coverage includes full tuition, a living stipend, round-trip travel, and limited support for research and internship-related costs. For example, APU requires scholarship requests by 15 September 2026 for April 2027 enrollment; other partner universities set their own comparable dates through early 2027.
how_to_apply: Choose a JADS partner university, apply for admission requesting JADS consideration, secure endorsement, and await AfDB selection; check each partner university's specific deadline.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Cape Town 2027 (Postgraduate)
organization: University of Cape Town & Mastercard Foundation
eligibility: Academically talented students from any African country (including Uganda) facing significant social and economic barriers, applying for their first postgraduate diploma, honours degree or master's degree at UCT.
summary: Comprehensive scholarships for the 2027 intake covering tuition, accommodation, living expenses, laptop, medical aid, visa and annual travel. Postgraduate applications close October 31, 2026.
description: UCT's partnership with the Mastercard Foundation supports young Africans who show academic excellence and leadership potential but lack financial means. Support is renewed annually subject to performance and participation in the Program's development activities. Undergraduate applications for 2027 are closed, but postgraduate applications remain open: applicants to an eligible Faculty of Health Sciences postgraduate diploma, honours degree or master's programme must submit the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application by 31 October 2026. Candidates should also satisfy UCT's admission requirements for their chosen programme.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an eligible UCT postgraduate programme, then complete the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program application form; email info_mfsp@uct.ac.za for queries.

title: University of Melbourne Graduate Research Scholarships - Round 1 for 2027
eligibility: Open to domestic and international students of all nationalities (Uganda included) applying for a graduate research degree (research master's/MPhil/PhD); automatic consideration when you apply for the course by the round closing date.
summary: More than 300 scholarships are offered to international graduate researchers annually, covering living stipends and full or partial tuition fee remission. The main Round 1 deadline for 2027 commencement is October 31, 2026.
description: The University of Melbourne automatically considers complete graduate research course applications received by round closing dates for Graduate Research Scholarships, which provide a tax-free living allowance and fee offset; some awards add health cover and relocation allowances. Health-related research candidates apply through the Faculty of Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences (MDHS). Round 1 applications for 2027 commencement close 31 October 2026 with outcomes notified around 18 December 2026; later rounds close 31 January and 15 May 2027. Deferred or currently enrolled researchers seeking reconsideration must submit a standalone form by 31 October.
how_to_apply: Find a supervisor, apply online for an eligible graduate research degree before 31 Oct 2026; scholarship consideration is automatic (a separate form applies only for deferred/enrolled students).

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarships 2027/28 (Round Opens September 2026)
organization: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
profession: All Subjects incl. Medicine & Public Health
eligibility: Citizens of any country outside the UK (Ugandans eligible) applying for a full-time postgraduate degree at Cambridge who demonstrate intellectual ability, leadership and commitment to improving the lives of others.
summary: Around 80 full-cost scholarships per year covering fees, maintenance, airfare and family allowance for master's and PhD study. Applications reopen September 2026 for 2027/28 entry; deadlines are December 8, 2026 or January 6, 2027 depending on course.
description: Gates Cambridge is one of the world's most competitive postgraduate scholarships, selecting on outstanding academic achievement, choice of course, commitment to social leadership and fit with Cambridge. About two-thirds of awards go to PhD candidates. Applicants apply for admission and funding simultaneously through the University's Graduate Application Portal, completing the dedicated Gates Cambridge funding section with a research/proposal statement and Gates reference. Applications open in September 2026; all non-US applicants follow course-dependent deadlines of either Tuesday 8 December 2026 or Wednesday 6 January 2027, with outcomes by December 2026 or March 2027 respectively.
how_to_apply: Choose a Cambridge course, apply via the Graduate Application Portal by the course funding deadline, tick Gates Cambridge in the funding section, and supply academic plus Gates Cambridge references.
key_dates: Applications open September 2026; deadlines Dec 8, 2026 or Jan 6, 2027

title: Clarendon Fund Scholarships 2027/28 - University of Oxford
eligibility: Open to applicants of all nationalities (no citizenship or residency restrictions) applying for a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil at Oxford by the relevant December 2026 or January 2027 course funding deadline.
summary: Oxford's largest scholarship scheme offers over 200 fully funded awards yearly covering all course fees plus a generous living-cost grant. No separate application - every eligible applicant is automatically considered.
description: Clarendon scholarships are awarded purely on academic excellence and research potential across all subject areas, with no quotas by nationality or degree level. To qualify, applicants must submit a complete graduate application (with references) by the December 2026 or January 2027 funding deadline shown on their chosen course page; later-round submissions are generally not considered. Awards cover full course fees for the duration of fee liability and an annual living stipend of at least GBP 15,009 for full-time scholars. Most applicants hear initial decisions between February and June 2027 for October 2027 start.
how_to_apply: Select an Oxford Master's/DPhil course, note its December or January funding deadline, and submit a complete Graduate Admissions application; no separate scholarship form is needed.

title: AfOx Graduate Scholarships / Mastercard Foundation AfOx Scholarships 2027/28 - Oxford
organization: Africa Oxford Initiative (AfOx), University of Oxford
profession: One-Year Taught Masters incl. Global Health
eligibility: African citizens ordinarily resident in Africa (incl. Uganda) who have not previously studied a master's degree and can demonstrate commitment to Africa's development; priority to historically underrepresented groups such as refugees and disabled students.
summary: Fully funded one-year taught master's scholarships at Oxford covering course fees and living costs plus tailored leadership training and networking. Consideration follows your Oxford course application by its December 2026/January 2027 deadline.
description: AfOx Graduate Scholarships go beyond fees and maintenance, offering pre-arrival, on-course and alumni support programs. Under the Mastercard Foundation partnership, up to three AfOx scholarships support the Said Business School MBA for 2027/28, while broader AfOx Graduate Scholarships cover eligible taught master's courses across the university. There is no separate scholarship form: candidates submit their graduate application by the earliest course deadline and eligible offer-holders are contacted to complete an AfOx questionnaire, followed by virtual interviews. Ugandan applicants in health policy, global health science, international health and tropical medicine courses have been strong fits historically.
how_to_apply: Apply to an eligible Oxford master's via the Graduate Admissions Portal by the course's December/January deadline; complete the AfOx questionnaire if invited after receiving an offer.

title: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS) - Intake 2027/28
profession: Public Health / Health Management / Infectious Diseases
eligibility: Graduates from developing/emerging countries (Uganda on the eligible-country list) with a bachelor's (usually four years) and at least two years of professional experience, applying to listed EPOS master's/PhD courses.
summary: Individual scholarships of 12-42 months covering monthly payments of ~EUR 992-1,400, travel, insurance and optional family/rent supplements for selected development-related postgraduate courses. Course-by-course windows run roughly August-October 2026 for the 2027/28 intake.
description: EPOS funds rigorously selected professionals from DAC-eligible countries to study internationally competitive master's and PhD courses at German universities closely linked to practice. Applications go directly to up to three chosen courses (listed in the official 2027/28 deadline brochure), never to DAAD itself, and selection runs from late October to March. Monthly stipends are EUR 992 for graduates and EUR 1,300-1,400 for doctoral candidates, plus health/accident/liability insurance, travel allowance and possible rent or family subsidies. Ugandan health professionals typically target courses such as International Health (Heidelberg), Public Health, Tropical Hygiene and hospital management programmes; exact deadlines differ per course, many falling September-October 2026.
how_to_apply: Pick up to three EPOS-listed courses, check each course's deadline in the official PDF list, and send DAAD EPOS forms, CV, reference letters and admission documents directly to the universities.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh 2027/28
profession: Global Health & Infectious Diseases / One Health (Online Options)
eligibility: African citizens resident in Africa (incl. Uganda), typically 35 or under at program commencement, with demonstrated academic talent, leadership potential and few educational opportunities due to financial constraints.
summary: Full scholarships for one-year on-campus master's degrees and three-year part-time online master's/postgraduate diplomas at Edinburgh. The 2027/28 cycle is expected to open mid-October 2026.
description: The Program invests in African leaders addressing climate and sustainability challenges; online offerings notably include MSc Global Health & Infectious Diseases, One Health, Biodiversity/Wildlife/Ecosystem Health, Data Science and Digital Education. Awards cover full tuition, living stipend (on-campus), laptop, travel and accommodation support, plus leadership development programming. Applications proceed in two stages: a Declaration and Eligibility Assessment due about a week before the main application deadline. Exact 2027/28 dates were not yet published as of August 23, 2026 - monitor the official page; aggregator reports indicate a first-stage deadline around October 19, 2026 and final deadline around November 19, 2026, unconfirmed.
how_to_apply: Watch the official page for the 2027/28 application link opening ~October 2026; complete stage-one eligibility assessment, then submit the full scholarship form with transcripts, degree certificate and references before the stated deadline.

title: Europubhealth+ European Master in Public Health - Erasmus Mundus Scholarships, 2027 Intake
organization: Consortium of 8 European universities led by EHESP
location: Multiple European universities (France, Spain, Belgium, Poland, etc.)
eligibility: Open worldwide (Ugandans eligible): bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS in relevant fields, English proficiency (B2/C1), with prior public-health experience scored favourably; scholarship applicants must apply in the first campaign.
summary: Two-year, 120-ECTS double-degree master's with compulsory mobility and seven specialisations; Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover participation fees plus up to EUR 1,400/month. The 2027 intake application platform historically opens early October 2026.
description: Europubhealth+ trains professionals to act on major public-health issues from epidemiology to health policy, awarding a joint/double degree after study across consortium institutions. Erasmus Mundus scholarships are only awarded in the first (January-deadline) campaign; results come mid-March with interviews for top-ranked candidates. Previous cycles confirm the pattern (e.g., 2026 intake opened October 8, 2025 with a scholarship deadline of January 8, 2026), but 2027 intake dates had not yet been announced as of August 23, 2026 - monitor the official application-procedure page. Expected scholarship deadline: early-to-mid January 2027.
how_to_apply: Prepare English test and documents now; when the emundus platform opens (~Oct 2026), register, upload transcripts, CV, references and motivation statement, and submit before the January scholarship deadline.

title: EMJM LIVE - Erasmus Mundus Master in Leading International Vaccinology Education, 2027-29 Cohort
organization: Consortium of five European universities (Lyon, Barcelona, Antwerp, etc.)
eligibility: Open to international students of all nationalities (Uganda included) with a bachelor's in biology, biochemistry, immunology, medicine, pharmacy or related life sciences; English proficiency required.
summary: Two-year joint master's producing graduates skilled in vaccine R&D and immunology, with Erasmus Mundus scholarships awarded to most admitted non-European students. Application window: November 19, 2026 - January 21, 2027.
description: LIVE provides advanced training in immunology, immunopathology, vaccine-targeted diseases, vaccinology legislation and health policy, with mobility across Spain, Belgium and France and internships via an industrial/academic network including big pharma and public-health institutions. The EMJM label lets the consortium grant scholarships covering participation costs, travel and living allowance to the majority of admitted European and non-European students. Applications must be submitted via the MyLIVE platform between November 19, 2026 and January 21, 2027 for both the one-year (M2) and two-year (M1+M2) tracks starting September 2027.
how_to_apply: Check prerequisites on the LIVE website, prepare academic records and language proof, then apply via MyLIVE during the Nov 19, 2026 - Jan 21, 2027 window.

title: DGD Scholarships - MSc Tropical Medicine / MSc Public Health / PhD at ITM Antwerp (2027-28)
organization: Institute of Tropical Medicine Antwerp (ITM), funded by Belgian DGD
profession: Tropical Medicine / Public Health / Laboratory Science
eligibility: Citizens of OECD-DAC low/middle-income countries (incl. Uganda) residing in an LMIC; early- or mid-career physicians, veterinarians, laboratory scientists and public health professionals meeting academic admission criteria; English proficiency required.
summary: Full or partial DGD scholarships covering tuition and living costs for the 60-ECTS MSc in Tropical Medicine, MSc Public Health (health systems & disease control orientations), short courses and sandwich PhD places. Deadline: January 15, 2027.
description: Applications for the 2027-28 academic year are open with a deadline of January 15, 2027 (courses run Sep 2027-Jul 2028). DGD also funds three-to-five PhD scholarships per year (up to 48 months, sandwich model) and specialised short courses in tropical medicine and international health. ITM is one of Europe's leading tropical medicine institutes with deep East African research partnerships, making it a natural fit for Ugandan clinicians and lab scientists. Candidates apply for admission first and download the DGD scholarship form during the application process.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the chosen ITM course and complete the embedded DGD scholarship application form by January 15, 2027, 23:59 CET.

title: Cambridge Africa Changemakers Scholarship (October 2027 Entry)
eligibility: Citizens of any African country applying for a full-time PhD at Cambridge; must tick 'Yes, I wish to apply for funding' in the Applicant Portal and meet course funding deadlines.
summary: Full-cost PhD scholarships (fees + maintenance) for students from any African country starting October 2027; the application cycle opens September 2026.
description: No separate scholarship form - consideration is automatic when you apply for admission and opt into funding by your course's funding deadline (typically early December 2026 or early January 2027 depending on the course; confirm exact date in the Cambridge Postgraduate Course Directory once the cycle opens). The Changemakers programme has supported African doctoral researchers across biomedical sciences, public health and clinical medicine. Combined with departmental funding, it offers a realistic route for talented Ugandan graduates aiming for UK PhD study.
how_to_apply: Apply for PhD admission via the Cambridge Applicant Portal when the cycle opens (September 2026), select funding, and ensure references arrive before the course funding deadline.
key_dates: Cycle opens September 2026; course deadlines Dec 2026 - Jan 2027

title: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme 2027/2028
eligibility: Citizens of partner countries (Uganda is a Sending Partner country) nominated per the bilateral framework; free tuition, dormitory/place allowance, health insurance and monthly stipend for the full programme duration.
summary: Flagship Hungarian government scholarship covering Bachelor's, Master's and PhD study; the 2027/2028 application period starts in November 2026, with submission expected around mid-January 2027.
description: Covers full tuition, housing support, medical insurance and monthly stipend. The 2026/27 round closed on January 15, 2026; the Hungarian embassy confirms the 2027/28 call has not yet been published. Medical, nursing, pharmacy and public health programmes at Hungarian universities are popular among African recipients. Applicants must also follow any Uganda Ministry of Education nomination requirements, so prepare early. Historically the portal opens in mid-November with a mid-January deadline (2pm CET).
how_to_apply: Create an account at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu when the November 2026 window opens; submit all documents by the published deadline (~January 15, 2027).

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters 2027 Intake - New Health Programmes incl. IDOH Next (Infectious Diseases & One Health)
eligibility: Students from any country including Uganda; bachelor's degree (min. 180 ECTS) in a relevant field; English proficiency; Partner-country (non-EU) nationals qualify for full EMJM scholarships.
summary: 37 new Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters were selected in July 2026 and begin accepting applications autumn 2026 for September 2027 start - including IDOH Next (Infectious Diseases and One Health) among other health-related programmes.
description: Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover participation costs plus a monthly contribution (~EUR 1,400) and travel/installation support. Most scholarship applications run October 2026-January 2027, but each consortium sets its own deadline; portals for newly selected programmes (e.g., IDOH Next - successor to the well-known IDOH programme with partners Universite de Tours, UAB Barcelona and Hannover Medical School) are being launched progressively. Ugandan graduates in biomedical, veterinary and public health fields are strong candidates for One Health-style programmes. Maximum three EMJM applications per candidate.
how_to_apply: Watch the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue and individual programme websites from autumn 2026; apply directly via each consortium's portal (max three applications per candidate).
key_dates: Applications open autumn 2026; most deadlines Oct 2026 - Jan 2027

title: Africa Epidemic Services (AES) - Epidemiology Track Fellowship 2026-2028
location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia + field placement in an AU Member State
eligibility: Citizens of African Union Member States (incl. Uganda) under 35 with a bachelor's or master's degree in public health or related field; government institution letter of support required.
summary: Fully funded two-year applied epidemiology fellowship for young African public health professionals, with stipend, travel, insurance and mentorship covered. Programme starts October 2026.
description: Africa CDC's flagship African Epidemic Service builds mid-level public health workforce capacity through three months of in-person training in Addis Ababa followed by 21 months of field-based applied epidemiology training in a Member State. Fully funded: monthly stipends, health insurance, accommodation-related support, learning materials and mentorship. This is a rare fully-funded entry point into the continental public health workforce for young Ugandan graduates.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the AU recruitment portal with the mandatory AU CV template, degree certificates/transcripts, two recommendation letters, motivation statement (max 500 words) and letter of support from a government institution by August 26, 2026.

title: Africa Epidemic Services - Public Health Informatics Track 2026-2028
profession: Public Health Informatics / Health Data Science
location: AU Member States (training and field placement within Africa)
eligibility: Citizens of African Union Member States (incl. Uganda) under 35 with bachelor's or master's degree; letter of support from Ministry of Health/National Public Health Institute or equivalent; proficient in an AU official language.
summary: Fully funded two-year fellowship combining public health training with health-information systems and informatics field practice across African Union Member States. Cohort starts November 2026.
description: Part of Africa CDC's African Epidemic Service flagship programme under Health Workforce Development, this track trains young professionals in public health informatics to strengthen disease surveillance and health information systems. Funding covers stipend, travel, insurance and learning materials. Ideal for Ugandan graduates interested in DHIS2, data science and digital health for outbreak detection and response.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application on the AU jobs portal with the mandatory AU CV template, degree certificate and transcripts, two professional reference letters, motivation statement (max 500 words), and institutional letter of support by August 26, 2026.

title: Virtual Global & Public Health Internship - Uganda
eligibility: Undergraduates, pre-health students, graduate students, and non-students with demonstrated interest in global/public health; English required; open to all nationalities including Ugandans.
summary: 4-week virtual internship exploring Uganda's approaches to HIV/AIDS, maternal and child health, nutrition and WASH through seminars led by Ugandan health professionals. Upcoming start dates from September 7, 2026; rolling admissions.
description: Participants dedicate 8-12 hours weekly to live Zoom sessions and interactive meetings led by CFHI's Kabale-based Medical Director and local NGO professionals, covering the Ugandan health system, infectious diseases, maternal/neonatal health and food security. Unpaid program (USD 975 fee; scholarships available); certificate of completion available. A strong option for students anywhere seeking structured exposure to Uganda's health system from global experts based in the country.
how_to_apply: Create a profile and submit the online application at cfhi.org/apply-program; program fee is due three weeks before start date.
key_dates: Rolling admissions; next start dates from Sept 7, 2026

title: Health and Nutrition Internship in Uganda (FOSCOD)
eligibility: University students and recent graduates in public health, nutrition, community development or related fields; full-time availability (30-40 hrs/week); minimum 4 weeks; open to all nationalities.
summary: Hands-on community health and nutrition placement with a grassroots Ugandan NGO running health, education and sustainability programs around Lake Victoria. Upcoming 2026 arrivals: September 26 and October 17.
description: Interns support FOSCOD's community wellbeing programs through health and nutrition outreach, patient/community education sessions, preventive care campaigns, monitoring and reporting. Homestay accommodation, meals, airport transfers, mentoring and a mid-program retreat included (fee-based placement); academic credit eligible. Suited to students seeking practical community-health field experience in a Ugandan district setting.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Roots Interns application form and share your CV at rootsinterns.com/apply; after matching, confirm with a USD 250 deposit.
key_dates: Rolling admissions; next arrival dates Sept 26 & Oct 17, 2026

title: Public Health Education Internship in Uganda (FOSCOD)
eligibility: Must be a university student in public health, community development, social work or related field; strong communication skills; full-time commitment (30-40 hours/week); minimum 8 weeks.
summary: Patient-education and preventive-care internship helping communities reduce avoidable hospital visits and adopt sustainable self-care practices. Next 2026 arrival dates: September 26 and October 17.
description: Interns conduct patient education sessions, monitor patient progress, develop accessible health materials, and support workshops and awareness drives with a Ugandan community-based nonprofit. Includes homestay with a host family, meals, local SIM/internet, orientation, training in project design and M&E, mid-program retreat and certificate (fee-based placement). Strong fit for public health students wanting grassroots health-promotion experience in Uganda.
how_to_apply: Complete the application form at rootsinterns.com/apply with your CV; shortlisted candidates have an interview call before placement confirmation.
key_dates: Rolling admissions; next arrival dates Sept 26 & Oct 17, 2026

title: UNHCR Internship Programme
profession: Humanitarian Work / Public Health / Data Management
location: Geneva HQ, Global Service Centre Amman, Budapest, Copenhagen + field offices worldwide (incl. Uganda operations)
eligibility: Current students (undergraduate with 2+ years completed, or graduate) or recent graduates (within 24 months) of an accredited university, any nationality incl. Ugandan; excellent English (B2+); no immediate family members working at UNHCR.
summary: Paid 2-6 month internships offering practical humanitarian experience with stipend, return travel reimbursement and visa assistance where no other support exists. Positions posted on rolling basis.
description: UNHCR offers eligible students and recent graduates experience in protection, public health, communications, research/data analysis, emergency response and program management aligned with their studies. Positions are posted on a rolling basis across global offices; interns who lack external funding receive a stipend covering basic living costs and local transport. Relevant for Ugandans interested in humanitarian health work, including refugee health operations such as those in West Nile settlements.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on the UNHCR recruitment portal, then apply online to specific open internship vacancies with CV and motivation letter; deadlines vary per posting.

title: CPHIA 2026 - Call for Abstracts & Travel Scholarships
organization: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
eligibility: Open to researchers, scientists, public health practitioners and implementers from Africa and beyond; abstract submitters may apply for consideration for travel scholarships. Ugandan health workers and researchers are eligible.
summary: The 5th International Conference on Public Health in Africa runs November 23-27, 2026 in Addis Ababa. Abstract submission closes September 15, 2026.
description: CPHIA 2026 is Africa's foremost public health gathering, convening political leaders, policymakers, researchers, innovators, civil society and youth around Africa's Health Security and Sovereignty agenda. The scientific programme covers health systems, workforce, financing, surveillance and innovation tracks. High-quality abstracts may be submitted for potential consideration for travel scholarships to attend the conference. Registration is now open, with invitation letters available upon registration for visa purposes. Presenting authors must register for the conference; final presentation uploads are due October 15, 2026.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the CPHIA abstract portal, prepare a ~300-word abstract aligned with conference tracks, submit by September 15, 2026, and register separately for the conference.

title: ICID 2026 - 21st International Congress on Infectious Diseases
eligibility: Open to clinicians, researchers and students worldwide; heavily discounted LMIC participant rates (EUR 350-450) and student rates are available, making it accessible for Ugandan health professionals.
summary: ICID 2026 takes place November 10-13, 2026 in Madrid with a One Health lens on clinical infectious diseases and microbiology. Regular registration closes September 30, 2026.
description: The 21st ICID brings together infectious disease specialists, clinical microbiologists, epidemiologists and public health experts to exchange knowledge across species and specialties under a One Health framework. The programme includes plenaries, symposia, workshops and poster sessions on endemic and epidemic diseases relevant to East Africa. Discounted registration categories exist for LMIC participants (EUR 350 early / EUR 400 regular) and students. Pre-congress workshops cost an additional EUR 100 for LMIC participants; onsite registration remains possible at higher late rates after October 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Register and pay online via the Kenes registration platform, selecting the LMIC or student category and uploading supporting documentation where required.

title: 10th Grand Doctors Conference & AGM 2026 (Uganda Medical Association)
organization: Uganda Medical Association (UMA), Teso Branch & Soroti University
eligibility: Open to medical doctors, researchers, health workers, policy makers, students and civil society; UMA members and non-members can attend. CPD points offered.
summary: The 10th Grand Doctors Conference and AGM runs November 13-14, 2026 at Soroti University under the theme 'Human Resources for Health - Harnessing the Numbers and Quality for Socioeconomic Transformation and Global Health'.
description: This national conference convenes Uganda's medical community for high-level scientific sessions, clinical skills workshops and networking, hosted by the Teso Branch and Soroti University. The 2026 theme focuses on health workforce numbers and quality for socioeconomic transformation and global health, highly relevant to Ugandan health workers. Delegates earn CPD points. Abstract/scientific session details and registration fees are published via UMA channels; interested participants should monitor the UMA website for registration links and deadlines.
how_to_apply: Register through the Uganda Medical Association events page or secretariat once registration opens; watch uma.ug for fee schedules and scientific submission details.
key_dates: Conference Nov 13-14, 2026; watch for registration opening

title: 11th AAU & ICSU Annual Scientific Conference 2026 (Anaesthesia & Critical Care)
organization: Association of Anesthesiologists of Uganda (AAU) & Intensive Care Society of Uganda
eligibility: Open to anesthesia and critical care professionals across Uganda and the wider East African region; affordable tiered fees for MOs, AOs, nurses and students (UGX 100,000-150,000 early bird).
summary: The premier regional anesthesia and critical care meeting runs October 14-16, 2026 in Mbale. Early bird registration closes September 30, 2026.
description: Now in its 11th edition, this conference gathers physicians, intensivists, nurses and allied health professionals to share research, exchange practices and strengthen perioperative and critical care in the region. Registration includes scientific sessions, tea breaks, lunch, a networking cocktail, exhibition access, conference materials and an e-certificate. International delegate rates range from USD 50 (students) to USD 150 (specialists) during early bird. The event offers strong networking for Ugandan health workers and regional colleagues.
how_to_apply: Register online via the AAU website and pay before September 30, 2026 to secure early bird rates; onsite registration is available at higher fees.

title: ICHOM 2026 Patient Scholarship Programme (Montreal Conference)
organization: International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement (ICHOM)
eligibility: Open to individuals with lived experience as patients or carers, representatives of patient advocacy organizations, and those affiliated with LMIC-based patient, research or non-profit healthcare entities - including applicants from Uganda.
summary: Scholarships support participation in the ICHOM 2026 Conference, December 7-9, 2026 in Montreal, removing barriers for LMIC voices in health outcomes measurement. Applications close September 17, 2026.
description: ICHOM's Patient Scholarship Fund provides complimentary or discounted registration (Standard Patient Pass valued at $650) plus travel and accommodation stipends based on financial need and distance travelled. The conference convenes global leaders in value-based healthcare and outcomes measurement. Priority goes to patients, carers and advocates, especially from low- and middle-income countries. Applicants must handle their own visas, insurance and logistics; funds must be used for conference-related travel and returned if attendance is cancelled.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Patient Scholarship application form by September 17, 2026; notifications go out from September 24, 2026.

title: ISPOR Europe 2026 Member Conference Travel Grant
organization: ISPOR - The Professional Society for Health Economics and Outcomes Research
eligibility: Active ISPOR members (non-students) residing in low/middle-income economies in Africa, Asia, Latin America, Central/Eastern Europe or Oceania, employed by academic, government or nonprofit organizations; no grant received in the past 5 years. Ugandan professionals are eligible.
summary: Travel grants provide complimentary registration plus fixed-amount travel reimbursement for ISPOR Europe 2026, held November 8-11, 2026 in Vienna. Applications close September 4, 2026.
description: ISPOR Europe is the leading European congress on health economics and outcomes research, drawing researchers, decision makers, payers and policy experts. The member travel grant aims to improve global representation from middle-income countries by covering full registration and reimbursing travel costs per ISPOR's reimbursement policy. Applicants must hold current ISPOR membership and work in academic, government or nonprofit institutions. A separate student travel grant exists for eligible students. Results communicated by September 25, 2026.
how_to_apply: Join/renew ISPOR membership if needed, then submit the online Member Conference Travel Grant application before the September 4, 2026 deadline.

title: 2027 Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation (Cycle 13)
eligibility: Individuals and teams who are citizens of and living in a sub-Saharan African country (including Uganda), aged 18+, with engineering innovations at an early stage of commercialisation; hardware needs a working prototype, software needs an MVP with user traction.
summary: Africa's biggest engineering innovation prize is open for its 13th cycle, offering GBP 50,000 top prize plus commercialisation support. Stage 1 applications close September 8, 2026 at 4pm UTC+1.
description: The Africa Prize awards crucial commercialisation support to innovators developing scalable engineering solutions to local challenges, including medical engineering, biotechnology and ICT innovations relevant to health. Shortlisted finalists receive training, mentoring, media exposure and lifelong alumni network access, with the winner taking GBP 50,000 and a 'One to Watch' award also available. The two-stage process begins with technical review of Stage 1 entries, then longlisted candidates complete a business-focused Stage 2 in October-November 2026. Shortlists decided by December 2026 and all outcomes announced by January 2027. Ugandan innovators have featured strongly in past cohorts.
how_to_apply: Access the Royal Academy's Grant Management System, select 'Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation 2026/2027 Stage 1', and submit the innovation details, endorsement letter, technical schematic and image by September 8, 2026.

title: EDCTP Prizes 2027
eligibility: Outstanding individuals and research teams from Africa and Europe working on poverty-related infectious diseases affecting sub-Saharan Africa; includes the Dr Pascoal Mocumbi Prize for individual achievement. Senior Ugandan researchers are eligible.
summary: Applications are now open for four EDCTP prize categories recognising excellence in global health research and innovation, with submissions accepted until September 2, 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time.
description: The EDCTP Prizes celebrate scientific leadership, collaborative team research and gender-balanced scientific contribution in research addressing infectious diseases in sub-Saharan Africa. Categories reward outstanding individual achievements (Dr Pascoal Mocumbi Prize), outstanding research teams working on diseases within Global Health EDCTP3 scope, and contributions to strengthening clinical research capacity and equitable North-South/South-South collaboration. Applications must be submitted directly by individuals or teams via the EU Funding and Tenders Portal and include recommendation letter(s) from at least one reputable scientist. Winners honoured at a high-profile ceremony in 2027.
how_to_apply: Prepare achievements summary and recommendation letters, register on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal, and submit the application directly by September 2, 2026, 17:00 Brussels time.

title: Wellcome Snakebite Innovation Prize (GBP 6.25M Challenge Prize)
location: Global (focus on snakebite-endemic regions incl. Sub-Saharan Africa)
eligibility: Open to organizations worldwide developing solutions to improve outcomes for people affected by snakebite; partners including Villgro Africa support innovators in most-affected regions during the entry phase.
summary: This GBP 6.25 million challenge prize improves outcomes for snakebite-affected communities across two tracks (Launch and Growth). Initial submissions close September 16, 2026 at 12 noon UTC.
description: Snakebite kills or maims hundreds of thousands annually, with the burden falling hardest on rural, poor communities in Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. The prize funds innovative solutions across diagnostics, therapeutics and care pathways through Launch and Growth award tracks. Entries opened June 17, 2026 and the strict initial deadline is September 16, 2026, followed by judging and finalist development into January 2027. Support partners such as Villgro Africa help region-based innovators prepare competitive entries. Highly relevant for African health-tech teams addressing neglected tropical diseases.
how_to_apply: Review prize rules and track criteria on the official site, register interest with support partners if needed, and submit initial entry materials before noon UTC on September 16, 2026.

title: NurseHack4Health Pitch-A-Thon 2026 (Track 2: Low/Mid-Resource Countries)
location: Global (Track 2 for low/mid-resource countries incl. Uganda)
eligibility: Interdisciplinary nurse-led teams within the same health system or nursing organization based in a low/mid-resource country such as Uganda; must be a registered nonprofit or international equivalent or have a fiscal sponsor.
summary: Competitive pitch program offering up to $175,000 (Track 2) of a total $400,000 pool for nurse-led solutions that strengthen the nursing workforce and care environments. Finalists pitch virtually on November 12, 2026. Applications close September 21, 2026.
description: The Pitch-A-Thon, presented by Johnson & Johnson, SONSIEL and Microsoft, seeks innovative solutions that create systemic, sustainable change for thriving nurse workforces and healthier work environments. Track 2 is explicitly reserved for health systems and nursing organizations from low to mid-resource countries, making Ugandan hospital/nursing teams eligible alongside US-focused tracks. Finalist teams receive coaching through an Innovation Accelerator (Oct 12 - Nov 6, 2026) before pitching to judges at a live virtual event on November 12, 2026. Funds must be used for project implementation with an executive sponsor, sustainability plan, and spending completed by end of the grant year. No IP is taken and there is no cost to apply.
how_to_apply: Attend one mandatory info/pitch-prep session, then complete the online application at apply.nursehack4health.org before September 21, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

title: GASOC PPH Innovation Competition 2026
eligibility: Open globally to individuals and multidisciplinary teams proposing practical innovations to improve prevention, management and outcomes of postpartum haemorrhage, particularly relevant to LMIC settings like Uganda. No finished prototype required.
summary: A global innovation competition seeking bold, practical ideas - devices, digital health tools, clinical pathways or training aids - to fight postpartum haemorrhage. Winner presents at the RCOG PPH Conference in London on October 5, 2026. Entries close September 15, 2026.
description: CRIBS International and GASOC launched this competition noting that a woman dies from PPH roughly every six minutes, with the burden concentrated in LMICs like Uganda. Entries can span medical devices, digital health solutions, clinical pathways, education/training tools or other approaches. Multidisciplinary teams are encouraged, and entrants do not need a finished prototype - a well-reasoned concept is acceptable, though more developed innovations may score better. Judging rewards practicality and feasibility in resource-constrained maternity settings. The prize includes a unique trophy crafted by Graham Tydeman (inventor of the Blood Clock), a 3-minute virtual or in-person presentation at the RCOG PPH Conference in London, and potential development support.
how_to_apply: Prepare a 3-minute video pitch of your PPH innovation and submit via the competition form linked from the CRIBS announcement before September 15, 2026.

title: Merck Foundation Media Recognition Awards 2026 - Diabetes & Hypertension
location: Africa (incl. East Africa/Uganda), Asia, Latin America
eligibility: Media representatives from African (including East African), Asian and Latin American countries; published/broadcast work promoting healthy lifestyles and awareness of diabetes and hypertension prevention and early detection.
summary: Annual media awards recognizing influential health reporting on diabetes and hypertension, run in partnership with African First Ladies. Winners receive US$500 per category. Submissions close October 30, 2026 via email.
description: The Merck Foundation Media Recognition Awards 'Diabetes & Hypertension' 2026 invite journalists across print, radio, online and multimedia platforms to showcase strong, influential messages that promote healthy lifestyles and raise awareness about prevention and early detection of diabetes and hypertension. The program is part of Merck Foundation's broader health-media capacity-building agenda across Africa. Ugandan health journalists are eligible under the East African category grouping. Multiple applications are explicitly encouraged. Winners are announced publicly via Merck Foundation's website and social channels.
how_to_apply: Email entries (published work plus required details) to submit@merck-foundation.com using the subject line 'Merck Foundation Africa Media Awards 2026 Diabetes and Hypertension' before October 30, 2026.

title: Global AMR Media Awards 2026 (3rd Edition)
eligibility: Open to all journalists and other media actors worldwide, including non-GAMA members; eligible content must have been published or broadcast between March 1 and October 15, 2026. Non-English entries need English translations.
summary: Annual awards honoring outstanding science-based reporting on antimicrobial resistance, with prizes in four regions including Africa. Deadline: October 15, 2026.
description: The Global AMR Media Awards, hosted by the Global AMR Media Alliance (over 300 media members from 33 countries), recognize journalists, bloggers, podcasters, broadcasters and social media creators who make the invisible threat of AMR visible through investigative reports, features, photo stories and other impactful communications. AMR contributes to nearly 5 million deaths annually and ranks among the top ten global health threats, making this highly relevant to Ugandan health reporters covering drug-resistant infections, prescribing practices and infection control. Regional prizes ensure African entries compete against peers rather than a single global field. Multiple entries permitted and judged separately. Winners announced during an online ceremony ahead of World AMR Awareness Week in November 2026.
how_to_apply: Complete the official entry form on amrmedia.org, upload proof of publication/broadcast and accessible audio/video files before October 15, 2026.

title: Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2027 (Expected Edition)
location: Global (open to registered nurses worldwide, incl. Uganda)
eligibility: Registered nurses anywhere in the world with significant contributions in patient care, nursing leadership, education, social/community service, or research, innovation & entrepreneurship in healthcare.
summary: US$250,000 global nursing award; the 2026 edition received 134,000+ registrations from 214 countries. The 2027 edition is expected to open nominations around September-November 2026 based on prior cycles - monitor the official site.
description: The Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award is one of the world's largest recognitions of nursing excellence, conferring US$250,000 on the winner selected via an EY-managed multi-stage process overseen by a grand jury of international healthcare leaders. Nurses self-nominate or are nominated in one primary and up to two secondary contribution areas, with applications accepted in multiple languages. The 2025 winner was Ghana's Naomi Oyoe Ohene Oti, demonstrating strong African representation. Based on prior cycles (2026 nominations opened September 10, 2025), the 2027 round is expected to open around September 2026. Ugandan nurses should monitor the official site and prepare achievement evidence in advance.
how_to_apply: Once nominations open, register/nominate at asterguardians.com or apply.asterguardians.com, selecting contribution areas and submitting supporting details in your preferred language.

title: Hult Prize 2027 Cycle (Student Startup Competition)
location: Global (campus, national, accelerator and London finals stages)
eligibility: Teams of 2-4 students enrolled in any degree-seeking university program worldwide, all aged 18+ by Feb 28, 2027; ventures must be impact-driven and SDG-aligned (health innovations qualify).
summary: The world's largest student startup competition awards US$1 million in seed funding to the winning team. Registration for the next cycle starts in September 2026.
description: The Hult Prize challenges student teams to build impact-driven startups tackling global issues through five progressive phases: campus/open-application qualifiers (September-February), national competitions (March-May), a digital incubator and accelerator, and global finals where one team wins US$1M in seed funding. Ugandan university students - including those in medicine, nursing, pharmacy and public health - regularly compete through campus programs or the open application route when their institution has no local event. Ideas addressing health-access challenges fit squarely within the SDG-aligned brief.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list at hultprize.org/en/register now; when registration opens (~September 2026), form a team, register online, and enter via your campus competition or the Open Application track.

title: MIT Solve Global Challenges - Next Round (2026-27)
location: Global (open to innovators anywhere, incl. Uganda)
eligibility: Tech-based social impact solutions from anyone, anywhere; the next round broadens eligibility to earlier-stage solutions, replacing topic-specific challenges with separate challenges per focus area (health among them).
summary: MIT Solve's open innovation platform will launch its next Global Challenges round in September 2026, with broader eligibility for early-stage teams. Selected Solvers join a funded cohort with access to >$1M in prizes, mentorship and a global support network.
description: MIT Solve sources tech-based solutions from nearly every corner of the world and connects selected Solver teams with funding, partnership and mentorship opportunities; past health-focused rounds included the Future Health Challenge and Philips Foundation Social Impact Award for maternal/child health and cardiovascular care. The recently closed 10th Anniversary Global Challenge states that the next Solve Global Challenges round will launch in September 2026 with separate challenges per focus area including health. Directly relevant to Ugandan medtech and digital-health ventures seeking catalytic funding and global visibility. Recent rounds included six-figure awards such as the $100,000 Philips Foundation Social Impact Award.
how_to_apply: Watch solve.mit.edu/challenges from September 2026; create a Solve profile, select the relevant health challenge, and submit an online solution application (pitch video, evidence of impact, scalability plan).

title: Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme - Next Cycle (2027)
eligibility: Founders across Africa with business ideas or young businesses (<5 years, <US$1M revenue typically) in any sector; selection favors innovative, scalable, job-creating ventures. Health-sector founders (clinics, medtech, digital health) are eligible.
summary: TEF provides US$5,000 non-refundable seed capital, 12 weeks of business training, mentorship and network access. The established pattern is a portal opening January 1 with a March 1 deadline - prepare now for the expected January 2027 opening.
description: The Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme is Africa's leading entrepreneurship philanthropy initiative, having funded over 24,000 entrepreneurs, trained 2.5 million Africans and created more than 1.5 million jobs since 2015. The 2026 cycle ran January 1 to March 1, 2026, with successful applicants currently completing seed-capital documentation. Historically the portal reopens every January 1, so Ugandan health entrepreneurs should prepare applications for the expected early-January 2027 opening. Selection is made by TEF and an independent committee against published criteria.
how_to_apply: Create an account on TEFConnect, complete the online application (idea stage or existing business track), and submit within the announced window - expected to open January 1, 2027.

title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) Uganda - 2026/2027 Cycle (Expected)
organization: Global Affairs Canada (High Commission of Canada)
eligibility: Local NGOs, community groups, non-profits, academic institutions implementing projects in Uganda; projects must align with Canadian thematic priorities including health under 'human dignity' and gender equality.
summary: CFLI funds small, high-impact projects (typically CAD ~20,000-50,000) designed and delivered by local organizations. The next Uganda call is expected around December 2026 - February 2027 based on previous cycles; monitor official channels.
description: The Canada Fund for Local Initiatives finances modest-sized projects conceived and implemented by local civil society, with priorities spanning inclusive governance, gender equality, peace and security, inclusive growth, environmental action, and human dignity (covering health, education and nutrition). Ugandan health NGOs have historically accessed the fund through calls managed by the High Commission of Canada, most recently the FY2025-26 call which offered grants of CAD 20,000-50,000. As of August 23, 2026, the 2026/27 Uganda call has not yet launched; interested organizations should monitor the CFLI index page and High Commission channels and prepare project concepts in advance.
how_to_apply: When the call opens, obtain the designated application form and budget template from the High Commission/CFLI page, complete them offline, and submit via the instructed email/portal before the stated deadline.
key_dates: Next Uganda call expected Dec 2026 - Feb 2027

title: Cambridge-Africa ALBORADA Research Fund 2026 Call
location: University of Cambridge (UK) + any African institution (incl. Uganda)
eligibility: Pairs of researchers: one at the University of Cambridge or an affiliated institute (e.g., Wellcome Sanger Institute) and one based at an African institution (any African country, incl. Uganda); post-doctoral level and above; all disciplines.
summary: Grants of up to GBP 25,000 (Research Catalyst) and GBP 15,000 (Workshop) to initiate or strengthen Cambridge-Africa research collaborations. The 2026 call closes September 3, 2026.
description: The ALBORADA Research Fund catalyses new and strengthens existing collaborations between researchers in Africa and Cambridge. Awards support research exchanges, joint projects, equipment and training workshops. Ugandan investigators with Cambridge links (e.g., through Makerere-Cambridge partnerships) can apply jointly for seed funding to develop grant proposals, run pilot studies or host capacity-building workshops. Strong stepping stone toward larger Wellcome/NIHR/EDCTP awards. Queries to alboradafund@cambridge-africa.cam.ac.uk.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the Cambridge-Africa website before the September 3, 2026 deadline.

title: ICGEB Fellowships in Pathogen Detection and Biosecurity (Africa) - September 2026 Call
organization: ICGEB (International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology)
location: ICGEB laboratories in Trieste (Italy), New Delhi (India) or Cape Town (South Africa)
eligibility: Nationals of African countries (incl. Uganda) affiliated with a research institute, university or public health laboratory in their home country; BSc(Hons)+ for Trieste/Cape Town, MSc for New Delhi; commitment to apply skills at home institution.
summary: Six-month funded training in pathogen detection, genomic surveillance, AMR, vaccine/biologics development and biosecurity, with monthly stipend (EUR 1,500 Trieste / US$1,122 New Delhi / ZAR 16,500 Cape Town). Full application stage: September 16-30, 2026.
description: Topics include molecular and point-of-care diagnostics, epidemiology and genomic surveillance, host-pathogen interactions, drug discovery, vaccine development, antimicrobial resistance, biosafety/biosecurity and biomanufacturing. Supported by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI) specifically for African scientists. Note: Expression of Interest stage closed August 14, 2026; shortlisted candidates submit full applications September 16-30, 2026. Ideal for Ugandan lab scientists and public health laboratory professionals seeking advanced molecular training.
how_to_apply: Shortlisted candidates (from the EOI stage) submit the full application through the ICGEB Service Gateway by September 30, 2026, 23:59 CET.

title: Pasteur Course: The Last Mile - Towards Elimination of Major Infectious Diseases (Feb 2027)
eligibility: Open international applicants working/studying infectious disease control; English-taught; counts toward Institut Pasteur Diploma and credits for the Pasteur-Cnam-EHESP Advanced Master in Global Health. Limited places (24 attendees).
summary: One-week intensive course (February 1-5, 2027) on control and elimination challenges for HIV, malaria, TB, polio, measles, hepatitis C and neglected tropical diseases. Registration deadline: November 27, 2026.
description: World specialists examine biological, socio-cultural and economic barriers to elimination of the 'big three' infectious diseases, polio, measles, HCV and NTDs such as rabies, filariases and sleeping sickness. Highly relevant to clinicians and programme staff working on disease elimination in Uganda and East Africa. Fees apply with possible support options; early registration recommended given only 24 places. Course completion contributes credits toward Institut Pasteur diploma programmes.
how_to_apply: Register online via the Institut Pasteur training portal by November 27, 2026; contact TLM@pasteur.fr for queries.
